questions.stem: In a rhombus PQRS, the diagonals intersect at M. Angle QPR = 35 degrees. What is angle PQR?
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect the vertex angles. So angle QPS = 2 x 35 = 70 degrees. Adjacent angles in a rhombus sum to 180 degrees, so angle PQR = 180 - 70 = 110 degrees.

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has all four sides equal and diagonals that bisect each other but NOT at right angles. What type of quadrilateral is it?
questions.explanation: A quadrilateral with all sides equal and diagonals that bisect each other is a rhombus. The diagonals of a rhombus always bisect each other at right angles. So a shape matching all conditions except right-angle diagonals is impossible.

questions.stem: In trapezium ABCD, AB is parallel to DC. Angle DAB = 115 degrees. What is angle ADC?
questions.explanation: AD is a transversal cutting the parallel lines AB and DC. Angles DAB and ADC are co-interior angles, so they sum to 180 degrees. Angle ADC = 180 - 115 = 65 degrees.

questions.stem: Which quadrilateral has exactly one line of symmetry and perpendicular diagonals?
questions.explanation: A kite has exactly one line of symmetry (along the main diagonal) and its diagonals are perpendicular. A parallelogram has zero lines of symmetry and non-perpendicular diagonals. A rectangle has two lines of symmetry but non-perpendicular diagonals.

questions.stem: One angle of a parallelogram is 72 degrees. What is the sum of the two angles that are NOT 72 degrees?
questions.explanation: In a parallelogram, opposite angles are equal. So the four angles are 72, 108, 72, 108 degrees. The two angles that are not 72 degrees are both 108 degrees, and their sum = 108 + 108 = 216 degrees.
